keys.description: The dev INBOUND mailbox's HTTP API (Mailpit). Dev-only by design — a hosted deployment replaces it with an IMAP / inbound-SMTP MailSource; nothing above the port knows which is in use
The PUBLIC API base the mailroom plans meetings on (the gateway). The mailroom is a consumer of the published REST surface, never of meeting-api internals
The Vexa API key presented as X-API-Key on every control-plane call. Unset (and not MAILROOM_DRY_RUN) ⇒ the poller does not run and /health says so, rather than crash-looping

address=workspace_id pairs, comma-separated. THIS MAP IS THE WORKSPACE RESOLUTION: an invitation naming a listed address belongs to that workspace, anything else belongs to nobody. Multi-workspace is this value getting longer
Single-pair shorthand for MAILROOM_WORKSPACE_MAP (with MAILROOM_WORKSPACE_ID) — the dev deployment configures exactly one address
The workspace id paired with MAILROOM_WORKSPACE_ADDRESS
Where the series↔meeting bindings, the resume cursor and the notice log are written (one atomically-replaced JSON file; mount a volume to survive a container replacement)
Seconds between mailbox polls. The series sweep (recurring bindings → next occurrence) runs on the same tick
Whether planned meetings are created armed (the bot joins at start time)
Decide everything, mutate nothing: parse, resolve and log what WOULD be planned without calling the control plane. The safe first run against a live gateway

keys.default: (unset — /internal is open on the loopback-bound dev port)
keys.description: When set, every /internal route requires it in X-Internal-Secret. The mailroom has no public surface and is not fronted by the gateway
Test-only: point the corpus eval at an out-of-repo .ics corpus (e.g. a date-shifted regeneration) instead of the vendored one
Bind address of the liveness/operator app
Deployment-declared Jitsi hostnames, read by the vendored meeting-link parser — the same key meeting-api declares, so an invitation's link resolves identically on both sides
